objective: Test whether the 17 CPVS residuals with both mean magnitudes and missing one band-specific period can be interpolated by a bounded, source-informed multiband Gaussian Process diagnostic.
previous_knowledge_consumed: The 11,602 residuals remain unexplained; no production selector change is authorized.
The shared-period phase-fold diagnostic run 43535760220 found that the 17-object subgroup has median coverage of 92/160 g bins and 91/160 r bins.
The 17 objects retain a positive common Table 2 period, both positive mean magnitudes and raw photometry in both bands.
The matched-control design uses one same-Type Table 4 member per residual, matched on common period, g/r magnitudes and Ng/Nr.

Chan et al. (2022), Section 2.1, specifies george MGPR, normalized phase/wavelength coordinates, separable RBF kernel, constant amplitude, diagonal white noise, zero mean, L-BFGS-B, three phase cycles and a 160-point output grid.

baseline.cohort: 17 candidate-only residuals with both mean magnitudes and one missing band-specific period; 17 deterministic matched Table 4 controls

change.proposed: Extend the bounded MGPR audit to eight deterministic L-BFGS-B starts per full-data object and four contiguous blocked-phase validation folds (four deterministic starts per fold), while preserving exact object/control identities and explicit output of optimizer and predictive diagnostics.
change.scope: Research-only script, tests and GitHub Actions workflow; no product dependencies, model, selector, feature schema, scientific threshold or baseline artifact changes.
change.rationale: The paper phase-folds both bands using the common Table 2 period. The 17 residuals have adequate observed phase coverage, so MGPR feasibility is the next discriminating experiment.

expected_improvement: Measure local-optimum sensitivity across eight full-data starts.
Measure sensitivity to the explicitly bounded kernel hyperparameters.
Evaluate held-out predictions in four contiguous phase sectors per object.
Report RMSE, MAE, normalized RMSE, one/two-sigma coverage and mean log predictive density.
Keep posterior uncertainty separate from out-of-sample predictive performance and membership evidence.

root_causes: The 17 residuals can be fitted numerically with the common Table2 period despite one missing band-specific period; a GP fitting failure is not supported as the explanation for these 17 catalogue exclusions.
The cause of the 11,602-object historical CPVS membership discrepancy remains unknown and is not resolved by this bounded MGPR experiment.
limitations: The paper does not publish exact initial values, optimizer bounds, George version or a complete reference implementation.
Two deterministic starts do not establish optimizer robustness; six objects show start-dependent NLL differences above 1.
Six residuals and nine controls reached the upper wavelength-metric log bound.
The full data were used for fitting and evaluation; no blocked-epoch or independent predictive validation was performed.
Posterior sigma is not a generalization-error estimate.
Zenodo g_flag/r_flag semantics are not assumed to equal DR2 catflags.
A converged GP fit does not prove historical CPVS membership.
The eight-start and blocked-phase extension has not completed; no out-of-sample metrics are available yet.

findings: The shared Table2 period supports finite two-band GP fitting for all 17 tested residuals despite a missing Per-g or Per-r value.
MGPR convergence is not a catalogue-membership criterion.
Posterior uncertainty and optimizer convergence must be separated from held-out predictive performance.
Two successful optimizer starts can still converge to materially different likelihood values.

Do not infer CPVS membership from MGPR fit or blocked-phase performance.

Investigate multi-start sensitivity and out-of-sample predictive performance.
